Alberta's iGaming Market Posts $122.1 Million in Revenue in Its First Three Months

Published October 25, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Alberta's newly regulated online gambling market generated CA$122.1 million (roughly US$87.2 million) in gross gaming revenue between its July 13 launch and Sept. 30, according to a report from the Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC). The figures give the first real picture of how quickly a competitive, multi-operator iGaming market can scale once it opens, and they land as other provinces and several US states continue weighing whether to allow more than one licensed operator at a time.

Revenue roughly doubled, then grew again

Monthly revenue climbed sharply across the market's first three full months: about CA$22.2 million in July, CA$43.3 million in August, and CA$56.6 million in September. Online casino games made up the large majority of that activity, accounting for roughly 75.6% of September's revenue, with sports betting at about 19.5% and live-dealer casino games making up the remaining 4.9%.

More operators came online fast

The number of licensed operators grew from 15 at launch to 24 by the end of September, and licensing activity kept climbing from there — the Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission had issued 42 iGaming licenses with 52 individual sites live as of Oct. 24. Active player accounts reached 388,585 in September, averaging roughly CA$146 in revenue per account for the month. Much of the continued growth in licensed operators appears tied to an Oct. 13 deadline the province set for previously unregulated sites to join the regulated market or stop serving Alberta customers.

Why it matters to a US bettor

Alberta joins Ontario as a Canadian province running a competitive iGaming model, where multiple licensed private operators compete for the same regulated customer base — a structure several US states have debated but not yet widely adopted for online casino gaming. The pace of Alberta's early growth offers a real-world data point for state lawmakers and regulators who are still deciding between a competitive multi-operator approach and more restrictive licensing models as they consider legalizing online casino gaming of their own.

Sources

  • Casino.org — "Alberta iGaming Revenue Hits $122.1 Million in First Three Months"
